data.name: Haran
data.gender_notes: Haran is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Haran is the name of a demon king who was vanquished by Lord Rama. The name Haran signifies 'one who removes' or 'one who takes away'. It is also a variant of the name Hara, which means 'thief' in Sanskrit. The name Haran carries the meaning “One who removes” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Haran usually hope their child will grow to embody one who removes and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the removal of obstacles and the victory over negative influences.
data.etymology: Haran belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who removes.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Haran total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Haran is a culturally significant name in Hindu mythology, For centuries, this name has been associated with power, strength, and victory. The story of Lord Rama and Haran serves as a reminder of the triumph of good over evil. It represents the idea that no matter how powerful or intimidating an adversary may seem, they can be vanquished through determination, courage, and devotion to one's dharma.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Haran signifies the idea of detaching oneself from worldly attachments and material possessions. The name reminds us that true liberation comes from within, by letting go of our ego and desires, just as Lord Rama let go of his attachment to his wife, Sita, in order to rescue her from Haran's clutches. It serves as a reminder that true peace and fulfillment come from within, and that we must continually strive to detach ourselves from the external world in order to connect with our inner selves and the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Haran signifies the one who removes or transcends worldly attachments, guiding us towards spiritual enlightenment. It symbolizes the release from the cycles of birth and death, as described in Hindu scriptures.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Haran is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the name of a king of Hastinapura. The name Haran carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Hastinapura was a major kingdom in ancient India and the capital of the Kuru dynasty. Haran is mentioned as a king of Hastinapura, but little else is known about him.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Haran continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
